title: Silicon solar cells could cut satellite power costs by up to 90%
source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
summary: Switching to modern silicon solar cells could cut the cost of powering satellites by as much as 90% based on beginning-of-life (BOL) performance, according to a review led by the University of Surrey. The switch to silicon cells could also halve the weight of the solar cells needed on a spacecraft, freeing mass for fuel or instruments or cutting launch costs.
